newsitem.title: LEBANON: 15 hurt in scuffles over naming Beirut prayer area.
newsitem.headline: 15 hurt in scuffles over naming Beirut prayer area.

text.p: Fifteen people were wounded in two days of scuffles between student supporters of two rival Shi'ite Moslem groups over naming a prayer area at the state-run Lebanese University in Beirut, security sources said on Tuesday.

They said one police officer and four policemen were hurt on Tuesday as they tried to break up the scuffles between supporters of the pro-Syrian Amal Movement and the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) in which four students were hurt.
Six people were injured in similar fights on Monday in which sticks, belts and empty glass bottles were used, they added.

The sources said the clashes broke out after Amal supporters insisted on naming a prayer room at the faculty of law "Amal martyrs' prayer area" while Hizbollah students wanted it named "Hizbollah martyrs' prayer area".
Police intervened on both days to break up the fights at the small campus near the office of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.
They arrested 11 people on Tuesday believed to have participated in the clashes in which the windshield of a police jeep was smashed, the sources said.
The faculty of law on Tuesday suspended classes indefinitely and ordered the closure of the prayer area which was established during the 1975-90 civil war when Moslem militias controlled west Beirut.
Amal and Hizbollah -- both vying for control of their strong Shi'ite community -- have frequenlty clashed during the war.
